summary: **Coordinating shift end procedures and work boundaries**
**Confirming shift end procedures and next day schedule**

item.text:
Bea finishes her lunch without turning the conversation into an interview. She wraps the remains, returns the accounts ledger to her canvas bag and carries the invoice folders into Nell’s office.

You go back upstairs.

The afternoon’s first task is to complete the business-paper box. You finish the open series, enter the location of the restricted staff file and leave three clearly worded query slips for Nell: one illegible date, one unidentified correspondent and one document whose connection to the former business cannot yet be established.

After Nell checks the completed section, she brings you a box of the cinema’s printed programmes from the 1990s.

“These are trust-owned under the same transfer schedule. Catalogue them as runs where you can. Individual records only when something materially differs.”

You preserve their existing order. Complete weekly runs stay together; missing dates are noted without explanation. Several programmes carry handwritten screening changes, ticket prices or printer’s marks. You describe those as annotations without assigning them to a particular member of staff.

One programme has a torn corner. Another shows a pale tide mark from old water exposure. A small group has been pierced for display pins. You record each condition without repairing, flattening or removing anything.

The work continues through the afternoon. Voices come and go below: Bea and Nell checking invoice totals, a delivery driver bringing the delayed crockery, the office telephone ringing twice. Nobody draws you away from the catalogue.

Shortly before four, Nell appears in the doorway.

“Finish the record you’re on. Don’t begin another.”

You complete the date range and condition fields, save the catalogue and return the programmes to their folder in the order you found them. The folder goes back into its marked box, and the box returns to its shelf. No loaned material has been used; the loan cupboard remains locked.

At four o’clock, the agreed end of your shift, the worktable is clear. You lock the archive room and enter your hours on the office timesheet.

Nell checks the time but does not add another task.

“Same start tomorrow. We’ll continue with the programme box.”

Your first full catalogue shift is finished.
